title: THE CURSE WE COULD NOT LIFT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Cursed is anyone who accepts a bribe to kill an innocent person.' Then all the people shall say, 'Amen!' 'Cursed is anyone who does not uphold the words of this law by carrying them out.' Then all the people shall say, 'Amen!'" — Deut 27:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The list of curses ends with a final, sweeping one that gathers up everything: "Cursed is anyone who does not uphold the words of this law by carrying them out." Read that carefully. It is not a curse only on murderers or idolaters. It falls on anyone who fails to keep the whole law. And all the people said, "Amen."

Do you see the weight of this? By agreeing to that final "Amen," the people were agreeing to a standard none of them could fully meet. Who among us keeps the entire law of God without a single failure? Not one. This last curse quietly exposes every person standing in that valley — and every one of us too.

The law, then, does something humbling. It shows us we cannot save ourselves. We stand under a curse we could never lift by our own obedience, because we cannot obey perfectly (Gal 3:10).

But this is where the gospel breaks in with breathtaking hope. Paul quotes this very verse and then declares that "Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us" (Gal 3:13). The curse we could never lift, Jesus lifted. He kept the law perfectly and then took its curse in our place. What Deuteronomy 27 leaves us unable to bear, the cross of Christ carries away. The chapter ends in curse; the gospel ends in redemption.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I recognise that I cannot keep God's law perfectly on my own?
2. How does the law's demand drive me to Christ?
3. Have I truly received the redemption Jesus won by taking my curse?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, I could never lift the curse of the law by my own obedience. Thank You for becoming a curse for me and redeeming me by Your cross. I rest wholly in You. Amen.
